question: How do I fix a leaky toilet fill valve?
answer: To fix a leaking toilet fill valve, first shut off the water supply to the toilet by locating the shut-off valve behind the toilet and turning it clockwise. Next, flush the toilet to drain the tank. Then, disconnect the water supply line from the fill valve and loosen the adjusting screw on the float arm. Pull the float arm down to adjust the water level, and then reassemble everything in the reverse order. Finally, turn the water supply back on and test the toilet for leaks.
steps: Shut off the water supply to the toilet
Flush the toilet to drain the tank
Disconnect the water supply line from the fill valve
Loosen the adjusting screw on the float arm
Pull the float arm down to adjust the water level
Reassemble everything in the reverse order
Turn the water supply back on and test the toilet for leaks
safety_info: When working with toilet tanks, be aware of the risk of electrical shock from the fill valve's electric eye. To mitigate this risk, turn off the power to the toilet at the circuit breaker or fuse box before starting work.
tips: Use a bucket to catch any water that may spill when disconnecting the water supply line
Consider replacing the entire fill valve if it's old or corroded
